answer: Agents can make every new identity post a refundable bond, then slash it when identities coordinate to claim the same scarce reward or violate a challenge rule. Honest agents recover their stake, while a Sybil operator must lock real capital for each persona and risks losing it, so multiplying accounts becomes costly rather than free. A saffron-market task at the wharf might use a crystal-clear duplicate-claim rule, making the penalty auditable without pretending the bond proves a unique human.
